dedupe_keys.name: 49 cfr part 192 transportation of natural and other gas by pipeline minimum federal safety standards ecfr

description: Title 49 of the US Code of Federal Regulations, Part 192, sets the minimum federal safety standards for transporting natural and other gas by pipeline, enforced by the Pipeline and Hazardous Materials Safety Administration (PHMSA) and published as an up-to-date electronic text (eCFR). Contents: sixteen subparts covering general rules, materials, pipe design, design of components, welding, joining, construction of transmission lines and mains, customer meters and service lines, corrosion control, testing, uprating, operations, maintenance, personnel qualification, gas transmission integrity management and gas distribution integrity management. Section 192.7 lists the industry standards incorporated by reference, 58 items when read, from bodies such as the American Petroleum Institute, ASME, the Pipeline Research Council International, the National Fire Protection Association and the Plastics Pipe Institute. Coverage: gas pipelines in the United States; the eCFR text was current to 25 September 2026, with amendments of April 2026. Format and access: HTML on eCFR and XML through the eCFR API. Licence and cost: free public law. Caveats: eCFR is an editorial compilation, not the official legal edition, and incorporated standards must be bought from their publishers. Its design factors, class locations and integrity rules set parameters and failure assumptions for hazard exposure and resilience models of gas pipelines. It relates to the PHMSA incident data and the National Pipeline Mapping System in the catalogue.
